harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created a CA named "Fleet Internal CA" on node1 (RSA 4096, self-signed, /etc/pki/fleet-ca), issued a SAN-bearing TLS server cert (CN=node2, DNS/IP SANs) signed by that CA, and installed it on node2 at /etc/pki/tls/fleet/. Configured node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 via a systemd-managed openssl s_server (-HTTP) service (fleet-https.service), enabled/persisted across reboot, with the firewall port opened. Installed the CA certificate as a trusted system anchor on both node1 and node2 via /etc/pki/ca-trust and verified with `trust list` and unqualified `curl` (no --cacert) succeeding on both nodes. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_ids and health, rebooted node1 then node2 sequentially via `systemctl reboot`, polled until each came back, confirmed changed boot_id on each, and verified post-restart recovery of CA trust anchors, node2's fleet-https.service (auto-started, active), and successful HTTPS verification from node1 to node2 using the system trust store.
actions_performed: Inspected OS/tooling on node1 and node2 (RHEL 7.9, openssl 1.0.2k, no repos/python3/nginx/httpd)

Created CA directory structure and generated 4096-bit CA key + self-signed x509 cert 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1 using a req config (basicConstraints/keyUsage) since -addext unsupported on old openssl
Generated node2 key + CSR with SAN (DNS:node2, IP:10.100.120.11) and signed it with the CA to produce node2's server certificate
Installed the CA cert into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors on node1 and ran update-ca-trust extract; verified via `trust list`
Wired cluster SSH (added CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to node2 authorized_keys, loaded CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY on node1) and scp'd CA cert + node2 cert/key to node2
Installed cert/key on node2 at /etc/pki/tls/fleet/, installed CA cert as trust anchor on node2, ran update-ca-trust extract, verified via `trust list`
Created systemd unit fleet-https.service on node2 running `openssl s_server -accept 8443 -HTTP` with node2's cert/key, serving a static response file; enabled and started it
Opened firewalld port 8443/tcp on node2
Verified end-to-end: curl from node1 to https://10.100.120.11:8443 succeeds using the system CA bundle (no --cacert), confirming both the served cert and the installed CA trust
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline on both nodes
Restarted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec available again, confirmed new boot_id, verified CA trust and node2 HTTPS reachability post-restart

Restarted node2 via `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec available again, confirmed new boot_id, verified fleet-https.service active, CA trust anchor present, and HTTPS working both locally and from node1

evidence.requirement: CA 'Fleet Internal CA' created on node1
evidence.summary: openssl x509 output shows self-signed cert with subject=issuer=/CN=Fleet Internal CA/O=Fleet

evidence.requirement: TLS certificate issued to node2 by the CA
evidence.summary: CSR generated for CN=node2; signed cert shows issuer=Fleet Internal CA and SAN DNS:node2, IP:10.100.120.11

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with the issued certificate
evidence.summary: systemd service fleet-https.service active running openssl s_server on 8443 with node2's cert; curl from node2 itself against the cert succeeds and returns 200

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: trust list shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor on node1; curl from node1 to node2:8443 succeeds using default system CA bundle (/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt), no --cacert override needed

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node2
evidence.summary: trust list on node2 shows Fleet Internal CA as anchor after update-ca-trust extract

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 738d0aac-71a1-4191-8a37-bf00edfeff5d and confirmed CA trust anchor present before reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot_issued' with connection closed by remote host confirming the restart was triggered

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proven
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id e328f319-e971-48bc-af1e-05df7bff829f differs from pre-restart 738d0aac..., proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery verified
evidence.summary: After reboot, CA trust anchor still present via trust list, and curl to node2:8443 over HTTPS succeeds using system CA bundle

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f, fleet-https.service active, CA trust anchor and cert/key files present before reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot_issued' with connection closed by remote host confirming the restart was triggered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: changed boot identity proven
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 02124884-ec7c-4ef3-8b5f-71841ed60fef differs from pre-restart 2fc81aed..., proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: post-restart recovery of TLS service and CA data verified
evidence.summary: After reboot, fleet-https.service is active (auto-started by systemd), CA trust anchor and cert/key files intact, and HTTPS verified successfully both locally on node2 and from node1 using the system trust store
